description:
pkix-ct/src/verify.rs:384-425

Return shape:

```rust
pub fn verify_embedded_scts(...) -> Result<usize>
```

- `Err(Error::NoScts)`: cert has no SCT-list extension OR extension
  is empty.
- `Ok(0)`: SCT-list extension present, has at least one SCT, but
  none of them verified.
- `Ok(N)`: N SCTs verified.

Every real caller is going to check "did we meet the policy
threshold?" which is `count >= 2` (CA/B Forum TLS BR §3.2.2.9) or
`count >= 1` (less strict). The caller writes:

```rust
match verifier.verify_embedded_scts(leaf, issuer) {
    Ok(n) if n >= threshold => Ok(()),
    Ok(_) => Err(MyError::InsufficientScts),
    Err(Error::NoScts) => Err(MyError::InsufficientScts),
    Err(e) => Err(MyError::from(e)),
}
```

The `Ok(0)` and `Err(NoScts)` branches collapse into the same
caller-side outcome. The asymmetry is API noise: one means "cert
declined to opt into CT" and the other means "cert opted in but no
SCTs verified" — but the caller almost never cares about the
distinction in production. They care about "did we hit threshold?".

Recommendation: add a higher-level method that does the count
threshold check:

```rust
pub fn verify_embedded_scts_meets(
    &self,
    leaf: &[u8],
    issuer: &[u8],
    min_count: usize,
) -> Result<()>
```

…that returns `Ok(())` iff `min_count` SCTs verified, else
`Error::InsufficientScts { found, required }` (a new variant).

Then `verify_embedded_scts` returning `Result<usize>` stays as a
diagnostic-grade method. The threshold method is what callers
actually use.

This pairs with PKIX-ppbr.6 (which flagged the same `usize` return
as opaque): if the diagnostic information is reported via a richer
result type (e.g. `SctVerificationReport { successful: Vec<&CtLog>,
failures: Vec<(SctId, Error)> }`), the threshold method becomes
"does the report satisfy the policy?".

Priority P2: this is defensive-forcing in the strict sense (every
caller writes the same threshold check) and also relates to the
diagnostic-opacity issue already filed.
title: verify_embedded_scts Result<usize> conflates NoScts error with count=0 — every caller writes if count >= policy_threshold && !is_err
